tweet_summary: Pubity claims 'a never-before-seen owl has been found in the USA,' a snowy owl nicknamed 'Rusty' with an unexplained reddish-orange appearance.
why_note_decision: A note is warranted because the headline claim — a 'never-before-seen owl' / new species — is false. But the original note is largely INCORRECT, so I flip the role from MissingKeyPoints to Incorrect. The real story: 'Rusty' is a SNOWY owl photographed in Huron County, Michigan in Jan 2025 (confirmed real by the Michigan DNR). It is NOT a new species; the leading explanations for its orange color are contamination (airport de-icing fluid or fire retardant), with a genetic-mutation hypothesis considered unlikely by most experts. The original note instead talks about EASTERN SCREECH OWLS exhibiting erythrism — the wrong species entirely (the bird and the tweet are about a snowy owl) — and asserts 'the second image is digitally altered' with no support, citing only an X handle. So the note misidentifies the species and makes an unsupported manipulation claim.
judge_guidance: A correct note must establish that (1) this is NOT a new/never-before-seen species — it is a known snowy owl ('Rusty') photographed in Huron County, Michigan in early 2025, confirmed real by the Michigan DNR; and (2) the orange color is unexplained but most likely external contamination (airport de-icing fluid or fire retardant), with a genetic mutation considered unlikely by most experts. PASS only if it rebuts the 'new species' claim and correctly identifies it as a snowy owl with the contamination/uncertain-cause explanation. FAIL if it repeats the original note's errors: attributing it to EASTERN SCREECH OWL erythrism (wrong species) or asserting an image is 'digitally altered' without support. Stating the cause is definitively a genetic mutation would also be wrong (experts lean toward contamination).
reference_note: This is not a new species. It is a snowy owl ('Rusty') photographed in Huron County, Michigan in early 2025 and confirmed real by the Michigan DNR. Experts say the orange coloring is unexplained but most likely external contamination — airport de-icing fluid or fire retardant — rather than a genetic mutation. https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/reddish-orange-snowy-owl/ https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/orange-snowy-owl-1.7486027

original_unhelpful_note.text: Eastern Screech Owls can exhibit erythrism, a documented genetic mutation causing reddish-orange feathers. The second image in this post is digitally altered, and no new owl species has been discovered or announced by wildlife authorities. https://x.com/HookandPine
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Incorrect: discusses EASTERN SCREECH OWL erythrism though the bird/tweet is a SNOWY owl; asserts 'the second image is digitally altered' without support; cites only an X handle. Only the 'no new species' clause is right; it omits the actual story (Michigan snowy owl, likely contamination).

fact_check.claim_verdict: Tweet's 'new species' claim false; bird is a real Michigan snowy owl, orange color likely contamination. Original note also wrong (wrong species, unsupported manipulation claim).
fact_check.notes: Real snowy owl 'Rusty', Huron County MI, Jan 2025, confirmed by MI DNR; leading cause de-icing fluid/fire retardant; genetic-mutation hypothesis viewed as unlikely. Replies independently flag the screech-owl/erythrism point as the wrong species.

importance.lens_rationale: 4.1M impressions on viral wildlife misinformation; from an animal-welfare/science-literacy lens, correctly identifying a likely-contaminated wild owl (a welfare concern) and debunking the 'new species' hype matters.
